My  class  structure  is  the  following:
●  Food:  The  most  general  class,  encompassing  all  edible  items.  ○  Ingredient:  Represents  any  component  used  in  food  composition.  ■  Bread  ■  Filling:  ●  Cheese  ●  Meat  ●  Vegetable  ○  Sandwich:  A  type  of  food  structurally  defined  by  bread  and  filling.  ■  ClassicSandwich:  A  defined  class,  exactly  2  breads  and  at  least  1  filling.  ■  Torta:  A  subclass  of  Sandwich,  with  the  optional  addition  of  sauce  and
spiciness.

My  properties  structure  is  the  following:
●  hasBread  ○  Connects  a  sandwich  to  its  bread  components.  This  property  is  functional,
meaning

a

sandwich

has

bread.
 ●  hasFilling  ○  Links  sandwiches  to  their  internal  content.  It  is  asymmetric  and  irreflexive,
ensuring

clear,

one-way

(a

sandwich

has

a

filling,

not

vice

versa).
 ●  hasSauce  ○  A  functional  property,  because  it  uses  one  kind  of  sauce.  It  links  to  Ingredient,  is
restricted

only

to

Torta,

and

any

be

an

ingredient.

 ●  isMadeOf  ○  A  general-purpose,  abstract  property  used  for  reasoning  over  all  compositional
parts.

ingredient

that

This  axiom  captures  the  minimal,  essential  structure  of  a  sandwich,  mirroring  common

●  Torta  Axiom:

○   A  Torta  is  a  type  of  sandwich  that  may  additionally  contain  sauces  and  spicy

This  definition  uses  only  rather  than  some  to  indicate  optional  use  of  sauces  and  spicy
elements

i.e.,

if

to

Though  any  of  the  axioms  I  do  not  explicitly  mention  isMadeOf,  all  the  properties  used
(hasBread,

hasFilling,

etc.)

are

sub

properties

Some  advantages  of  my  approach  are  the  following  points:
1.  Clarity  and  Precision:  Clear  structural  constraints  allow  for  unambiguous  reasoning
about

sandwich

makeup.
 2.  Extensibility:  The  class  and  property  structure  can  be  expanded  to  include  new
sandwich

types,

ingredients,

preparation

methods,

or

dietary

restrictions.
 3.  Modular  Design:  Clean  separation  of  components  (bread,  fillings,  sauces,  spiciness)
facilitates

reuse

in

broader

food

ontologies.
 4.  Reasoning  Support:  Logical  property  characteristics  support  automatic  inference  and
classification

by

ontology

reasoners.

At  last,  some  disadvantages  of  my  approach  are  the  following  points:
●  Limited  Scope:   The  focus  on  structural  composition  excludes  other  types  of  similar
foods

such

as

wraps

or

flatbreads,

which

may

be

considered

sandwich-like

but

do

not

fit

the

exact

bread-and-filling

definition

used

here
 ●  Lack  of  Ingredient  Individuals:  While  ingredient  categories  exist,  individual  ingredients
(e.g.,

cheddar,

jalapeño)

are

not

yet

modeled.
 ●  Scalability  Complexity:  Adding  preparation  steps,  serving  contexts,  or  dietary
annotations

would

require

significant

ontology

growth.
